findings.text: General page table range walk normalizes the caller supplied interval outward to page boundaries, opens the supplied walker, traverses from the configured start level, always closes the walker after traversal, and returns setup failure or traversal outcome.

Traversal iterates top level slots then descends level by level. Each entry is examined once, offered to a pre order table callback or leaf callback when the walker enables it, re read after the callback to observe concurrent replacement, then either advances the cursor past the leaf granule or recurses into the child table followed by an optional post order callback. Any callback status that the continuation predicate rejects ends the walk.

Walks reject intervals extending beyond the implemented address size and reject missing roots. Invalid level values are rejected. Slot positions are derived from masked address bits shifted by per level granule width, with a distinct top level derivation using one level coarser width. Inner iteration stops at range end and outer iteration advances across top slots until covered.

An entry is treated as a table only when below the last level, marked valid, and carrying the table type value. Child table access translates the entry address through the memory operations indirection supplied to the walk.

A retry status from a visitor is treated as permission to continue only when the walker opted into ignoring it, which accommodates races where the fault condition disappeared. Other nonzero statuses terminate traversal while zero continues.
Before invoking any visitor callback for a shared walk, the implementation checks that the appropriate external guard is held, with stage two read side protection cited as an example.

Hypervisor leaf protection requires readability and rejects writable executable combinations and device executable combinations. User execution is dropped when hypervisor execution extensions are absent. Device selects device memory type while normal memory selects regular type, with shareability, accessed flag, and software bits applied, and privileged versus user execute never controls programmed according to extension availability.

Stage two setup validates address range, allocates a table descriptor, initializes it through a protected mode aware dispatcher, and records ownership. Duplicate setup is silently accepted for nested contexts but rejected for the canonical context. Non protected guests additionally allocate per CPU last runner tracking and page split cache state, record the root physical address, and initialize nested bookkeeping when applicable.

Address width selection uses the global limit for protected guests. Explicit virtual machine types are validated against the global limit and the architectural minimum. Unspecified types fall back to the physical shift with a one time warning and failure on over limit. The resulting width plus sanitized feature registers determine the virtualization control value.

Virtualization control composition starts from fixed flags, encodes physical range and a size offset derived from sixty four minus address width, enforces a minimum of two levels, encodes the start level, and conditionally enables hardware access flag handling, large address extension handling, and wide virtual machine identifier handling.

Stage two teardown destroys the full implemented address space in granule aligned chunks with voluntary rescheduling between chunks, then destroys the root. Higher level release clears the recorded root and table pointer plus per CPU tracking under exclusive guard, resets nested state when nested, and performs actual reclamation after releasing the guard.
Detachment of the stage two table pointer and clearing of related bookkeeping occur under the virtual machine memory write guard, with nested context reset also performed while holding that guard.

Host virtual machine setup reserves a hypervisor handle and records protection state, warning and tainting once for experimental protected type. Teardown serializes on the configuration guard, finalizes teardown when the guest was created, otherwise unreserves a reserved only handle, then clears handle and creation flag and releases teardown caches. Creation state is read plainly relying on external serialization.

Nested stage two reset marks the translation base with the copy not private bit as an invalid sentinel, disables nested stage two, and zeroes the reference count. Nested table allocation sizes the pointer array by maximum virtual CPUs times contexts per CPU, and teardown frees each group head and the array while resetting size.

Host to hypervisor unsharing is skipped in native hypervisor mode, when the host owns hypervisor mappings, or for an empty source. The range is processed page by page with a warning on failure that leaves the page shared, noted as a leak that preserves isolation and is unexpected in practice. Kernel address translation validates direct mappings and combines the vmalloc page base with page offset for vmalloc addresses.

Virtual machine destruction releases performance filter and CPU mask resources, destroys the interrupt controller, tears down the protected guest when enabled, releases stage two and multiprocessor identifier data, frees register masks, destroys virtual CPUs, unshares the host image, destroys nested state, and tears down hypercall filters.

Multiprocessor identifier release holds the configuration guard while detaching the pointer under read copy update protection, waiting for a grace period, then freeing. Interrupt controller destruction acquires slot guard then configuration guard, destroys debug, per CPU and distributor state, releases the configuration guard before unregistering version three redistributors, then releases the slot guard. Redistributor release and direct interrupt teardown each require the configuration guard held.

Virtual machine debug setup exposes stage two table, address range and level views plus an optional nested directory when hardware supports nesting, alongside identifier register and exception residue views.

Distributor teardown clears ready and initialized flags, frees shared peripheral interrupts and resets counts and bases, frees each redistributor region and clears per virtual CPU back pointers for version three or resets the CPU interface base otherwise, tears down direct interrupt state when supported, and destroys the logical peripheral interrupt index. Debug teardown is an empty operation.

Direct interrupt support is always true for the fifth generation controller. For earlier generations it depends on message and software generated interrupt paths gated by global version four presence, interrupt translation service presence, version four point one hardware plus CPU interface support, and per virtual machine capability. Message support is suppressed when software generated interrupts are hardware supported but not enabled for the guest.

Direct interrupt teardown is a no operation without allocated virtual processing elements, otherwise it clears status flags and releases each associated interrupt before freeing translation resources and clearing bookkeeping. Helper selection chooses plain or protected prefixed implementations based on protected mode. Early interrupt setup initializes the logical peripheral interrupt index with interrupt safe locking.

Observed page table state includes address width, root pointer, start level, memory operations and owner back pointer; walk cursor includes interval bounds, current position and walker reference; walker includes flags, argument and callback; visit context carries entry pointer, sampled value, range, level and flags.
Virtual CPU fault entry always reports a bus error to the caller.
